messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#608] Re: rmr 2.1 Sorts Key Incorrectly
messages.body_plain:
You don't seem to be familiar with the concept of a Hash Partitioner. That's the default in mapreduce (independent of rmr) and because of that keys get randomly scattered around. Plus R objects are just raw bytes to Java, so whatever Java sorting does to them, it's not what you would expect. But in any event it's within reduce groups, not global. If you need global sorting, like in the terasort paper, you need custom partitioners (in that case a Range Partitioner). Unfortunately rmr2 doesn't support those yet. If you know how to implement them, please send your patches our way.

Antonio

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#612] Re: Integrating R and Apache Hama
messages.subject_clean: [RHadoop:#612] Re: Integrating R and Apache Hama
messages.body_plain:
Hama is a BSP computing engine on top of HDFS, and YARN is a resource
manager, which manages the cluster resource allocation and multiple
(e.g., MapReduce, BSP, MPI, Spark) jobs.

See also, http://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/hama/trunk/docs/diagram/yarn-hama-diagram.pptx

In my humble opinion, BSP and MPI should be used as a main parallel
computing engine of R, instead of others (Iterative MR or Spark).

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#615] Re: rmr 2.1 Sorts Key Incorrectly
messages.body_plain:
This is what I found
The order Hadoop produces is a raw byte order (all R data goes through Hadoop as raw bytes). Because of the specific serialization used, the strings are sorted short to long first, then alphanumeric within the same length. To verify this, you can run a job with the number of reducers set to 1, but with reduce = NULL argument to mapreduce. This will use a Java identity reducer.
2.0.2 hides this sort order in smaller examples, but it can't for bigger ones where not all data can be read in memory at once, which is actually the general case. 2.1 never hides this because the last key is processed separately.
A way to have Hadoop follow a more natural oder for at least the simplest types would be to write a custom comparator in Java that skips the first 5 bytes which contain type code and length. I read reports that somebody did something similar for the Dumbo project, with which we share the serialization format, but they didn't share the code.

Antonio

Is there a good example of where the BSP model is strictly more general than spark? It seems to me there should be such a thing because spark persisted data sets are read only, albeit possibly in distributed memory. For instance, with the kmeans example, that Thomas Jungblut (HAMA committer) uses on his blog, you really can't appreciate the difference between the two models, because each iteration takes in input an immutable large set of points and a smaller, mutable, broadcast set of centers. Of course there must be also some fault tolerance tradeoffs with unrestricted mutability, I am trying to wrap my mind around HAMA-503 but it will take more time.  Thanks

Antonio

messages.body_plain:
Maybe I have to learn more about Spark's programming model and its mechanism.

BTW, it looks like Spark had been not tested on real large cluster yet
-- "The original input file is around 1G, and the job will take up as
much memory as we allocate.  I have had it consume 180G per working on
4 workers."[1]

Unlike data-intensive text processing, I think almost
scientific/mathematical algorithms have one characteristic in common:
Input is relatively small but computational complexity is big. So,
we're focus more on spilling (MEM + Disk hybrid) messaging queue and
partitioning algorithms for distributing workloads of graph or matrix
computations than performance.

1. https://groups.google.com/d/topic/spark-users/3gmk3zdEZ7w/discussion

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#619] Remote R access to a cluster running RHadoop
messages.subject_clean: [RHadoop:#619] Remote R access to a cluster running RHadoop
messages.body_plain:
Yes, you need to configure Hadoop to work that way and rmr2 will pick up that configuration. How this is accomplished exactly depends on your Hadoop distribution but it boils down to two things: you desktop needs to have Hadoop installed; the configuration "points" to your cluster, providing the necessary server names or addresses and ports. Please refer to the installation instructions of whatever Hadoop distribution you are using. If you can run hadoop jobs from the command line, you should be able to run them also with rmr2, as long as the two environment variables, HADOOP_CMD and HADOOP_STREAMING are properly set, something you have done already for your test run and you should repeat on your desktop. Keep in mind that if your desktop is a windows machine, windows support has just been announced by Hortonworks and we are not able to support rmr2 on windows yet.

Antonio

messages.subject_clean: [RHadoop:#633] Re: RHadoop repo split into package repos
messages.body_plain:
There's two issues here. submodules, which I explored for other goals and decided against (we use subtree instead). Read the first few matches of this <https://www.google.com/search?aq=f&oq=git+submodules+problems&sourceid=chrome&ie=UTF-8&q=git+submodules+problems&qscrl=1> and it is pretty disappointing. So let's take submodules out of your proposal and replace it with subtree, which seems to address many of the objections to submodules. Why would we do that? You are talking about distributions. Each commit of the main repo would  not be a distribution because neither are commits of the separate repos. The only distributions are the tar.gz files linked to from  the Downloads page, not because we love red tape, because we can't have hundreds of versions around and we can't test after every commit on every supported platform. Without that motivation, I have myself considered having the central repo with the other repos as subtrees, but the only reason I had was that it is technically possible and keeping them up to date, unfortunately, is a manual task. Another thing to do, another thing to forget. So right now I am for the DRY principle, the code is in one place, not in two. Of course there may be other advantages I am unaware of. Thanks

Antonio

messages.subject: Re: Is there a good IDE for Rhadoop debuging?
messages.subject_clean: Is there a good IDE for Rhadoop debuging?
messages.body_plain:
There is no IDE for RHadoop as much as there isn't for any other R package. RHadoop is not a language so it has no IDE. For debugging, see the https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki/Debugging-rmr-programs for rmr and for all packages use the regular debugging features in R (debug, recover and trace). For RStudio, I am not sure what it means that it doesn't work -- I have a slightly different opinion about that as I use it every day. They have a wonderful support staff reachable at support.rstudio.org <http://support.rstudio.org>. But you have to give them more to work on, "it doesn't work" isn't really actionable.

Antonio

messages.subject: Cleaning Up temp Files
messages.body_plain:
All,

The tutorial <https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/rmr2/blob/master/docs/tutorial.md> mentions at several points that big data objects clean up after themselves when the data is no longer needed. For example, "to.dfs can put the data in a file of your own choosing, but if you don't specify one it will create temp files and clean them up when done."

However, when I run the following simple example, I see that some temp files are created in hdfs://localhost:9000/tmp, but the are not cleaned up (even when I close R later):
small.ints = to.dfs(1:1000)
rm(small.ints)

Thanks,
M

Thanks a lot for the fix.

Now I have two follow-up questions.

1) Is it possible to somehow change the settings such that a different directory is used by rmr2 for the temp files instead of the /tmp directory? I'm asking since I have set up two users, one for Hadoop admin ("hdadmin"), the other one ("hduser") for using Hadoop (e.g. with rmr2). Currently I have set dfs.permissions to false in conf/hdfs-site.xml, otherwise hduser has sometimes problems  writing to /tmp. So I think it would be better if I could, for example, have rmr2 use /user/hduser/tmp for temporary files instead of /tmp. This way I would not have to disable the enforcement of HDFS file permissions.

2) Now rmr2 seems to clean up the files in the temp directory it has created (/tmp/RtmpmRxrvP in the example above). However, when all variables in this directory are gone and thus all temp files have been created, the temp directory /tmp/RtmpmRxrvP still persists. I am aware that this might be so because if some new big data object is created, you don't need to create another temp directory. On the other hand, over time, this might clutter the /tmp directory. Of course, it possible to simply manually delete everything in /tmp every now and then, but I am wondering whether it is possible to also clean up the /tmp/RtmpmRxrvP folder.

Anyway, thanks for your excellent work with RHadoop.

Best,
M

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
the implementation of the hadoop backend is based on hadoop streaming. Rscript with a number of arguments is supplied as the -mapper, -reducer and -combiner options (the latter two when necessary) accepted by hadoop streaming. It is conceivable to provide additional arguments and options to Rscript, so if it also accepts the options you are interested in setting, then it can be done, but not in the current version of rmr. Please enter an issue in the issue tracker and give a little bit of motivation or a use case for this request. Thanks

Antonio

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#653] Locale Settings
messages.body_plain:
This is quite odd, all those dates are "coming from hadoop" generally speaking, albeit different components. The one that is generating the YY/MM/DD format is

$HADOOP_CMD jar $HADOOP_STREAMING dumptb path-to-data

dumptb is not a particularly well known feature of streaming added with HADOOP-1722

So to test if this has anything to deal with R (I expect it won't, but let's try to build some evidence) you can do from R

to.dfs(1:10, output = some-path)

Then at the cmd line

$HADOOP_CMD jar $HADOOP_STREAMING dumptb some-path

You should see the same messages in console. If that's the case, my guess is that your log4j configuration on the master machine and the nodes is different. In that case I may have to redirect you to a dedicate hadoop user forum where  people with deeper expertise can weigh in.

Antonio

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm trying to implement a rmr2 code to transform a edge list to a sparse adjacency list for an undirected graph on a map reduce environment...

The input is similar to this example:

1 2
1 3
2 3
3 4
6 5
5 3
9 6

and the output required is this:

1 2 3
2 1 3
3 1 2 4 5
4 3
5 3 6
6 5 9
9 6

I'm trying to do it with this following code but I'm not getting there. I'm still learning how to work with RHadoop so any advise on this is much appreciated.

#! /usr/bin/env Rscript
Sys.setenv(HADOOP_CMD="/usr/bin/hadoop")
 Sys.setenv(HADOOP_HOME="/usr/lib/hadoop-0.20/bin")
 Sys.setenv(HADOOP_STREAMING="/usr/lib/hadoop/contrib/streaming/hadoop-streaming-0.20.2-cdh3u5.jar")

library(rmr2)
map <- function(k,v) {
   fields <- unlist(strsplit(v, "\t"))
   keyval(k=unique(c(fields[1], fields[2]),if(fields[1]==k){v=fields[2]}else{v=fields[1]}))
}

reduce <- function(k,vv) {
   keyval(k, (unlist(vv)))
}

kvtextoutputformat = function(k,v) {
paste(c(k,v, "\n"), collapse = "\t")
}

mapreduce(
input = "Tests.txt",
output = "output-RHadoop",
#textinputformat = rawtextinputformat,
#textoutputformat = kvtextoutputformat,
output.format='text',
map = map,
reduce = reduce)

Thanks

I am not sure I can follow your code, but the problem is well understood, so this is how I would go about it for directed graphs:

```
from.dfs(
  mapreduce(
    to.dfs(
      data.frame(
         from = sample(1:5, 10, T),
         to = sample(1:5,10,T))),
    map = function (k,v) keyval(v$from, v$to),
    reduce = function (k,vv) keyval(k,list(vv))))
```

of course for a random graph, but I think it's better to keep parsing issues out of the logic  of the graph algorithm.  If this makes sense, great, otherwise feel free to shoot some questions back. Thanks

Antonio

The issue we are facing with the beta cluster and a larger 50 machine hadoop cluster with R streaming job is that the R, code which is compute intensive and memory intensive, seems to be garbage collecting. These machines are 32 core machines, and what we find is that the system cpu% goes to 70% where as the user cpu% is low.  When profiled, using "perf", i noticed that there was lot of spinlock within the kernel which is inducing the system cpu% to go up massively, there be rendering the machine to be less effective for other jobs.

We do know that the code does lot of rbind [ without proper data type mapping], and lots of memory allocation in a tight loop , but before attempting to fix the code, wanted to spawn the R program with "--min-vsize=512M --max-vsize=1G --min-nsize=500k --max-nsize=1M" and see if that reduces the system cpu%.  So is there a way to set this currently ? . Let me know if you need more inputs.

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#653] Locale Settings
messages.body_plain:
As a general comment, I think developers should take responsibility for the problems of the libraries they choose, so sometimes we do address bugs in hadoop as if they were rmr2 bugs, see #2 and #16. I think it depends on how crucial these problems are and how specific to the way in which rmr2 uses Hadoop. The logging format, that seems totally unrelated to the way rmr2 and Hadoop interact. But it's a case by case call whether we should fix something or punt it to the Hadoop community or vendors, and I' am not going to pretend I always know what the best approach is.

Antonio

messages.subject_clean: How to get RHadoop working in Rstudio
messages.body_plain:
Rstudio doesn't pick up settings in your .bashrc file. You can set the necessary environment variables with Sys.setenv. See also a related discussion <http://support.rstudio.org/help/discussions/questions/1072-renviron-and-bashrc>. I hope this helps

Antonio

messages.body_plain:
Thanks for clarifying that. Then I am thinking it must be a time out. I think that should show in the web UI if you click on the failed tasks. Since you've been on that page to get to the logs I am going to assume that no error was reported there, which is not consistent with a time out. The message is in a table and says "Task attempt_201303171013_0002_m_000000_0 failed to report status for 600 seconds. Killing!". Also I noticed that the mapR UI looks a little different so you need to translate whatever I say for that platform. Other than that I am at a loss. You could try and source the file mapreduce.R in the tests directory in the source package that has a variety of tests that start jobs but are less intensive then the once in benchmarks.R, and see if that passes. That would support the idea of a timeout. Thanks

Antonio

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#691] RHadoop license statement
messages.body_plain:
R packages come with a DESCRIPTION file where the license is indicated as Apache 2.0. All source code files also carry the same statement, with the occasional omission that is fixed promptly. I am no legal representative for the copyright holder, but you can verify these claims yourself. I hope this helps and good luck with your auditors.

Antonio

On Monday, March 25, 2013 1:46:42 AM UTC-7, Vladimir Starostenkov wrote:
> Hit the same issue. But I do have the root pass.
> Installed rmr2, rhdfs from sources in the following way:
> $cd /home/<username>
> $git clone https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/rmr2.git

One comment about cloning. We changed our git workflow to follow what the git project does more closely (as opposed to git flows). So if you check out the project like this you get the current master which is somewhere between the current release and the next hotfix release. There is no guarantee how well tested that is. It's a stable version plus fixes, so that should be good, but we can't run the full battery of tests for every commit. The other thing is that you are going to run a non released version, somewhere in between 2.1.0 and 2.1.1, so if you need support it may be hard. So I encourage you to clone the project if you are not running in production, but if you experience problems, I suggest you go back to the latest stable. Thanks

Antonio

messages.subject: clustering algorithms
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
in the dev branch of rmr2 under pkg/examples I added an initial implementation of a single pass clustering algorithm <https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/rmr2/blob/dev/pkg/examples/mclust.mr.R> based on mclust. The idea, inspired by similar ongoing work in  the Mahout project, is to cluster data as early as possible in reasonable chunks and then merge the results. With a generative model like the one generated by mclust, one merger strategy is pretty obvious: simulate datasets from each of the partial clusters, take the union and cluster again. I found mclust hard to use though or downright incomplete. It searches for the best number of clusters using exhaustive search between 1 and 9. Specifying a different range doesn't seem to work very well, at least the plots are incomplete and anyway a complete algorithm should not rely on magic parameters. Imagine if a software engineer delivered a sorting algorithm that works up to length 9 or needs additional input. If anybody has experience with mclust or can suggest a clustering algorithm of wide applicability, efficient and model based that would be very helpful. Also if anybody is working on clustering large datasets and wants to take this algorithm for a spin (as soon as the nagging issues are fixed, right now I can break it by myself) I'd appreciate the feedback.

Antonio

messages.subject: Re: clustering algorithms
messages.body_plain:
Well, apparently mclust and I don't get along very well, but I made some progress in two directions
1. When an algorithm fails, build a framework. Since frameworks can't run, they can't fail. So I wrote a generic mapreduce clustering function that takes a clustering function and cluster merging function as arguments.
2. Since the above is cheating, I instantiated the framework based on the clustering function clara, which, unlike mcclust, works. That made the mapreduce version work as well. Unfortunately, one needs to specify the number of clusters in advance and the compute time seems to rise quite drastically with the number of clusters.

The file is cluster.mr.R under examples in the branch dev for now. That alone should be a reminder that this code is highly experimental. Enjoy

Antonio
